notes: When saying what something is full of, полный takes the genitive case (полный воды — 'full of water') and often uses the short forms полон, полна, полно, полны.
Do not confuse with целый ('whole', 'entire'), which stresses that something is intact or undivided (целый день — 'the whole day').

senses.definition: Containing as much or as many as possible; having no empty space.

examples.text: На столе стоял полный стакан воды.
examples.translation: A full glass of water stood on the table.

senses.definition: Having all its parts; not lacking anything; total or absolute.

examples.translation: This is the complete list of all participants.
examples.emotion: confident and certain, reviewing a final document

senses.definition: Of a person or body: slightly overweight; having a rounded build.

examples.text: Это был невысокий, немного полный мужчина.
examples.translation: He was a short, slightly plump man.

notes: Полный can mean holding as much as possible, entirely complete, or describing a person who is somewhat chubby.
Do not confuse полный with целый (whole/entire), which focuses on something remaining undivided.

senses.definition: Containing as much or as many as possible; holding nothing more.

examples.translation: The glass is full of water.
examples.emotion: careful and steady, holding a cup to the brim

senses.definition: Containing all the necessary parts; complete.

examples.translation: This is the complete list of all participants.
examples.emotion: confident and certain, reviewing a final document

senses.definition: Having a stout or chubby build.

examples.translation: He is a somewhat chubby person.
